1.explanation:
1. src/js/themes/default.js – contains the default theme definitions for radioButton.check.background.color; necessary to see how the default styling is applied and how your override is merged.
2. src/js/components/RadioButton/README.md – documents the theming API and shows what properties RadioButton supports, so you can confirm you’re using the right keys.
3. src/js/components/RadioButton/RadioButton.js – the core implementation reads theme.check.background; reviewing it reveals whether the background style is conditioned on the checked state.
4. src/js/components/RadioButton/stories/CustomThemed/index.js – demonstrates applying a custom theme in a live example; you can reproduce the issue and experiment with fixes.
5. src/js/components/RadioButtonGroup/README.md – explains grouping behavior and how selection is managed; sometimes the group propagates styling.
6. src/js/components/RadioButtonGroup/RadioButtonGroup.js – implements the logic for rendering multiple RadioButtons; inspecting it helps ensure only the checked item receives the custom background.
1.bug_scenario: The user has applied a custom theme to Grommet’s RadioButton component, setting the check.background.color to “#3b5ed8”. However, instead of only the checked radio button receiving that blue background, all radio buttons render with the blue fill—even the unchecked ones. In the screenshot there are three radio buttons: the first should remain default grey, the second (checked) should be blue on white, and the third unchecked should be grey again—but all three appear blue-filled. The problem lies in how the theme’s check.background.color is being applied indiscriminately rather than conditionally when the RadioButton is checked.
